head: claude/mi93-pr-author-live-refusal
title: manager: refuse a PR action while its author session is still live (MI-93)
body:
## What this is

The **refusal half** of `DEC-20260902-HOW-A-MANAGER-IS-HELD-TO-ITS-MANDATE` -> `both`. MI-89 built the derived read (`manager_view.py`, #10896); this is the refusal that uses it. Cycle priority `CY-20260903-MANAGER-CONTROL`.

**The motivating event is measured, and I verified it against primary sources rather than the dispatch.** `docs/claude/CYCLE-PRIORITY.json :: current.why` clause (3), operator-set 2026-09-02:

> "The manager undrafted and armed #10857 while its author was still RUNNING, because there was no way to ask -- and nothing objected."

Confirmed on the PR itself via `pull_request_read`: #10857 (`claude/mi83-per-merge-ping`) created 2026-09-02T20:46:36Z, merged 21:59:16Z. The same clause names the shape of the gap — *"a RUNNING session cannot be reached, an IDLE one CAN be woken, and nothing tells the manager which it is."*

Now something objects.

## The load-bearing split: what is derived live, and what is read from the register

The register is measured **wrong about state** and is the only thing that knows **identity**, so the two come from different places on purpose:

| | source | why |
|---|---|---|
| **LIVENESS** | **only** a live `list_sessions` observation | `SESSIONS.json::state` is stale by construction — MI-84 measured **17 of 17** inherited `working` rows wrong, MI-89 re-measured **24 of 24** register assertions contradicted by a live read. A refusal keyed on stored state would refuse on stale data and be switched off within a day. |
| **IDENTITY** | the PR body's own footer, then the register's branch/PR association | A branch-to-session association is an **immutable historical fact** — session X opened branch Y, and that does not decay the way `state: working` does. This is the tool's main assumption and it is stated in the docstring so it can be argued with, not buried. |

Identity is preferred **from the PR itself**, which is better than either: `create_pull_request` bodies carry a `claude.ai/code/session_{id}` footer written by the authoring session at open time. It travels with the PR, cannot go stale, and needs no register.

**MEASURED 2026-09-03, population: ALL 8 open PRs on this repo, via `list_pull_requests`** — 5 of 5 `claude/**` PRs carry the footer (#10900, #10895, #10893, #10888, #10877; #10895 carries it twice, identically); 0 of 3 `automation/**` PRs do, correctly, since a workflow-opened PR *has* no author session.

## Which way `unknown` fails — decided, and argued

`unknown` is its own verdict with its own exit code (4). **Neither a soft pass nor a hard refusal**, and both alternatives were rejected for stated reasons:

- **Not a hard refusal.** A gate that blocks whenever it cannot look would block on a paginated `list_sessions` page, a missing flag, or a reformatted PR body. The manager would learn to pass a bypass on every invocation and the gate would be decorative inside a day — the same call `spawn_gate.py` made.
- **Not a soft pass.** It exits non-zero, prints at refusal volume, and can never be reported as `permitted`.
- **And it is cheap to clear *here*, which is why it is tolerable.** The manager holds `list_sessions` and `list_pull_requests`. In CI — which holds no `mcp__*` tools — `unknown` would be **permanent**, and a permanently-amber check is one everyone learns to walk past. A permanent `unknown` and a one-flag-away `unknown` are different things, and only the first breeds alarm fatigue.

**Also: absence from the observation is not death.** `list_sessions` is paginated — a page is not a population — so an author not on the supplied page grades `unknown`, never `permitted`. Reading "not on this page" as "finished" is precisely how this would be routed around by accident.

## It must not stall work that is genuinely done

A session can be alive *and* finished — today three went idle with PRs ready. Two paths PERMIT with no exception needed:

1. **The author handed back.** A `review_ready` / `needs_action` / `blocked` / `awaiting` status is the author's own declaration that the PR is the manager's now. This is checked **BEFORE liveness, so it outranks it** — a RUNNING session that has said "over to you" has already answered the only question this gate asks, and the whole point of clause (3) is that there was *no way to ask*. Refusing a session that answered unasked would be ceremony.
2. **The author is idle or terminal.** An idle session **can be woken** — the operator-stated remedy, not a blocker.

So it refuses exactly one condition: **an author observed live that has not handed the work back.** The #10857 condition and nothing wider. The refusal text names the author, names all three ways forward, and puts "ASK IT" first.

## Where it lives, and why not the two obvious alternatives

- **Not a CI guard.** CI cannot call `list_sessions`, so it could only ever grade `unknown` on the one input the question turns on. `manager_preflight.py` records the same reasoning for its own manual-only wiring.
- **Not a check inside `manager_preflight.py`.** Preflight asks *"may this manager act AT ALL?"* — fleet-wide, no target. This needs a **target PR** as an argument, and folding a target-taking check into a target-less tool would force every existing preflight run to grade it `unknown` for want of an argument, turning a working tool amber on day one. `spawn_gate.py` is the precedent: a per-action gate at the moment of the action.

Its `--self-test` **is** wired into CI (`run_guards.py :: manager-tooling-selftests`) — pure planted-failure cases over pure functions, no clone depth, no network, no MCP, so it is depth-independent like its three siblings and cannot red a PR for an environmental reason.

## The escape hatch is a file, not a flag

`docs/claude/work/pr-action-exception.yaml`, in `spawn-priority-exception.yaml`'s shape and graded by **`spawn_gate.exception_covers` — the same function, imported rather than re-implemented**, so the two cannot drift on what an approval means. `decision: pending` still refuses; an approval with no `approved_by`/`approved_at` is a session approving itself; it covers only the PRs it NAMES.

**There is deliberately no `--force`.** A bypass flag is cheaper to lie to than to satisfy — the `new-table-wiring-guard` lesson. The shipped file is `decision: pending` with `covers: []`, so it grants nothing, and a test asserts that.

## Verified against a LIVE read, not fixtures

Population: **all 8 open PRs** and a **100-row `list_sessions(mine=true)` page** (91 idle, 6 archived, 3 running), 2026-09-03T~07:2xZ.

| PR | author | live reading | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| #10895 | `session_018ruZ...` | **running** | **REFUSED** (exit 3) |
| #10900 | `session_01Q1HY...` | idle | permitted |
| #10893 | `session_017TRS...` | idle | permitted |
| #10888 | `session_01AYPx...` | idle | permitted |
| #10902, #10398 | — | `no_author` (automation) | permitted |

**That live run found a real defect the 40-case planted-failure suite could not, and this is the part most worth carrying.** Every self-test case built its PR entry **by hand**, so all 40 passed while the CLI graded **every one of the 8 live PRs `unidentified`** — it fed the payload through `manager_view.normalise_prs`, which projects onto four fields and drops `body`. A suite that constructs its own inputs cannot catch a broken input path. Pinned by six new self-test cases (including one that runs a raw `list_pull_requests`-shaped payload end to end) and a CLI test in pytest.

## On `manager_view.py` — I did not widen another session's contract

Widening `normalise_prs` to keep `body` was the first fix I tried and is the **wrong** one: MI-89's `manager_view._self_test` asserts that function's output by **exact dict equality**, so adding a key would fail that session's suite (which `run_guards.py` runs) to serve a need its tool does not have. `pr_action_gate.open_pr_entries` recovers the two fields instead, and says so in its docstring. `manager_view.py` is untouched.

## Verification

- `pr_action_gate.py --self-test`: **46 cases pass**, and the suite runs on **every invocation**, not behind a flag — machinery that just failed to verify itself does not get to grade a manager.
- `tests/test_pr_action_gate.py`: **38 passed**.
- `python3 scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base main`, run **after** committing: **PASS 83 - FAIL 0 - SKIP 0** — "All relevant guards passed."
- `ruff check .` clean — under the **pinned 0.15.8**, not the 0.16+ that a bare `pip install ruff` pulls; `requirements-dev.txt` bounds it `<0.16` precisely because 0.16 expanded the default rule set, and the unpinned binary reported 86 findings on my file *and 26 on the untouched `spawn_gate.py`*.

### What I could NOT run, and am not reporting as green

- **`layer-guard` needed `import-linter`**, absent from this container. I installed it rather than reporting the guard unrun: **6 contracts kept, 0 broken**. The `PASS 83` above is the run after that install; the first run was `PASS 82 - FAIL 1` with `lint-imports` exiting 127.
- **The full pytest suite.** Only `tests/test_pr_action_gate.py` was run; many test modules in this repo need `pandas`/`numpy`/`fastapi` which are absent here. My change imports none of them and adds no runtime code path.

## What this does NOT establish

**Shipped is not observed.** No manager has run this gate against a real action. Its `--self-test` runs in CI from the moment this merges; the **gate** is manual-only and binds nothing until a manager invokes it. I have not added an `OPEN-ITEMS.json` row — the register is contested and I did not want to conflict with a sibling session mid-flight; the manager should add one if it wants the unproven half tracked.

It also does not judge whether an action is the **right** one, only whether the author may be interrupted; and it cannot tell whether a live author is still editing *this* branch — nothing reachable links a running session's activity to a branch, so a live author is treated as reachable-and-possibly-working, the pessimistic and safe direction.

## Landing

**Tier-1, `landing: "self"`**, armed with `.github/pr-automerge-requests/mi93-pr-author-live-refusal.txt`.

I first wanted `hold` — this gate constrains the manager, and the manager merges. I talked myself out of it, and the guard is why: `hold_reason` is a **closed vocabulary** and none of the five fits *"Tier-1 but I would feel better if someone looked"*, which is exactly the adjectival hold the closure exists to refuse. Everything here is inside `TIER1_SURFACE`, nothing is `LANDING_MACHINERY` (so R12 does not bind), and merging binds nobody — the gate is manual-only. **The board START post therefore went on a separate branch** (`claude/mi93-board-start`), since `automation/**` is outside the Tier-1 surface and would have failed R5 — and because a board-post result commit landing last on this branch would leave this PR with zero check runs, the trap CLAUDE.md records hitting #10680 twice.

If the manager would rather read it first, flipping to `hold` is a one-line edit to the landing file.

Opened through `pr-opener.yml`: `create_pull_request` returned `403 Resource not accessible by integration` for this session, with `get_me`, `pull_request_read` and `list_pull_requests` succeeding as positive controls.
